text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- 18 Finns died in midsummer holidays: eight in holiday traffic, four by drowning and five in violence.
- President Martti Ahtisaari celebrates his 60th birthday in various receptions around Helsinki.
- Aboub 80 Finns are imprisoned outside the Nordic countries, mainly for drug related crimes, an official at Foreign Ministry says. @
- Some Finns celebrated midsummer by skiing in Kuusamo, where Ruka ski slopes still have a snow cover of four metres.
- Finding a suitable business partner is vitally important for Finnair ; CEO Antti Potila says airline does not want to limit itself to a one-area company.
- Despite vast amount of community tax revenues expected, municipalities are still planning cuts in salaries and holiday pay as well as staff lay-offs. @
- Regional telephone company Helsingin Puhelin is said set to be listed in the Helsinki stock exchange next autumn; worth five billion markka, Finnish analysts say.
- Finnish electricity transfer company Suomen Kantaverkko, jointly owned by power companies Imatran Voima (IVO) and Pohjolan Voima, sets up credit lines ahead of planned independent operation.
- Long-service conscripts will get higher daily allowance, Defence Minister Anneli Taina says on plans to restructure military service. @
- Increase in apartment prices has ceased after a strong rise in recent months.
